docs.title: Spring AI Session Extensions
docs.text:
Add-ons for the session support in Spring AI 2.1.

Spring AI 2.1 has the session itself: the event log, the stores, the ChatClient advisors, compaction and recall. This project adds features on top of it and changes nothing in it. It uses only the public extension points of the session: event types of its own, version-checked appends, and advisors around the session advisors.

Note

Experimental. Nothing is released yet. The API can change between versions.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
Module Artifact Description Session Turn spring-ai-session-turn Turn state for a session, kept as events in the session log. No dependency on the ChatClient. Session Turn Advisor spring-ai-session-turn-advisor The ChatClient binding of the turn: an advisor around the Spring AI session advisors. BOM spring-ai-session-extensions-bom Bill of Materials for the module versions.

Turn Status explains the turn service, and Turns in the ChatClient the planned ChatClient binding.

Stores beyond the ones in Spring AI go into the session-repositories folder of the project. A store is built here first and moves into Spring AI when it is stable.

docs.title: Turns in the ChatClient
docs.text:
Planned

This page describes the design of spring-ai-session-turn-advisor. The module is not built yet. The turn service it uses is available.

spring-ai-session-turn-advisor runs every ChatClient call as a turn. It starts the turn before the call and ends it after. When the tool loop pauses on a tool call that needs a confirmation, it parks the turn instead of ending it. A later call with the person's decisions resumes it, on any instance.

docs.title: It wraps the Spring AI advisors
docs.text:
Spring AI 2.1 already has session advisors for the ChatClient. This module does not replace them. It adds one advisor in front of them and leaves them as they are.

Advisor Order Runs The turn advisor of this module HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE + 100 Once per call, first Spring AI SessionTurnAdvisor HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE + 200 Once per call: creates the session, compacts Spring AI ToolCallingAdvisor HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE + 300 The tool loop: runs tools, pauses on a confirmation Spring AI SessionMemoryAdvisor HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE + 1000 Once per model call: stores the messages, builds the prompt

A lower order runs further out. So the turn advisor sees the whole call, and it sees the response after the Spring AI advisors stored it.

The turn advisor does three things the Spring AI advisors do not:

  • It records the turn. start before the call, end after, park when the response is a paused reply.
  • It resumes a parked turn from decisions. The request carries the person's decisions and no user message.
  • It closes a pause when new text arrives. It stores a denial for each open tool call before the text goes on. The log then says the calls were denied, not that they have no result.

docs.title: A paused tool call and its resume
docs.text:
Two calls. The first one pauses on a tool that needs a confirmation. The second one carries the decisions and finishes the turn.

sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Application
    participant T as Turn advisor
    participant TS as TurnService
    participant S as Spring AI advisors<br/>(turn, tool loop, memory)
    participant M as Model

    A->>T: prompt "Book flight VX205"
    T->>TS: start(sessionId, runId)
    T->>S: request
    S->>M: prompt with the stored history
    M-->>S: reply: call bookFlight
    Note over S: memory stores the reply,<br/>tool loop pauses: bookFlight needs a confirmation
    S-->>T: paused reply
    T->>TS: park(sessionId, runId, ToolConfirmationQuestion)
    T-->>A: paused reply, awaiting a decision

    Note over A: the person decides, later,<br/>maybe on another instance

    A->>T: prompt with decisions, no user message
    T->>TS: resume(sessionId, runId, decisions)
    T->>T: run the allowed calls<br/>through the ToolCallingManager
    T->>S: request: the tool results only
    Note over S: memory stores the results after the reply
    S->>M: prompt: the turn so far and the results
    M-->>S: "Your flight is booked."
    S-->>T: answer
    T->>TS: end(sessionId, runId, END_TURN)
    T-->>A: answer

On the resume, the turn advisor sends the tool results as the request. Spring AI's turn advisor sees that the open calls have results and leaves them alone. Spring AI's memory advisor stores the results right after the reply, and the model gets the whole turn.

docs.title: What the turn advisor decides on each call
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A([A call arrives]) --> B{Is the session parked?}
    B -- no --> C[start the turn]
    B -- yes --> D{Does the request carry decisions?}
    D -- yes --> E[resume with the decisions,<br/>run the allowed calls,<br/>send the results on]
    D -- no --> F[resume with every call denied,<br/>store the denials,<br/>send the text on]
    C --> G[Forward to the Spring AI advisors]
    E --> G
    F --> G
    G --> H{Is the response a paused reply?}
    H -- yes --> I([park the turn on the question])
    H -- no --> J{Did the call fail?}
    J -- no --> K([end with END_TURN])
    J -- yes --> L([end with ERROR])

A request with decisions on a session that is not parked is refused. A busy session, one on which another turn runs, refuses the call with TurnInProgressException.

docs.title: Turn Status
docs.text:
A turn is one piece of work a harness does on a session: from a user's message to the model's last answer, with every tool call in between. spring-ai-session-turn records in the session's log whether a turn runs, under which run id, and why the last one ended.

This solves three problems that a plain conversation log has:

  • Two harnesses can run one session at the same time. Two instances, or two browser tabs, append their messages in between each other's. With a turn status, the second one is refused.
  • A running turn cannot be stopped from elsewhere. A stop button on another instance has nothing to write to. With a turn status, it records an interrupt that the running harness reads.
  • A turn that waits for a person is lost on a restart. A tool call that needs a confirmation pauses the turn, and the pause lives only in memory. With a turn status, the question is in the log, and any instance can resume the turn with the answer.

The module works with any Spring AI session store, because it uses only what every store has: events of its own type, a read by type, and a version-checked append.

docs.title: Using it
docs.text:
TurnService turns = new TurnService(sessionService);

TurnStatus turn;
try {
    turn = turns.start(sessionId, runId);
}
catch (TurnInProgressException ex) {
    return busy(ex.getRunId());                     // another turn runs: refuse, a 409 for example
}
catch (TurnParkedException ex) {
    return ask(turns.pendingQuestion(sessionId));   // the session waits for an answer
}

try {
    // run the turn: call the model, run tools, append messages
    turns.end(sessionId, turn.runId(), StopReason.END_TURN);
}
catch (RuntimeException ex) {
    turns.end(sessionId, turn.runId(), StopReason.ERROR);
    throw ex;
}

busy and ask stand for what your application does. A refused start writes nothing and owns no turn. That is why it stays outside the second try: there is no turn to end.

From anywhere else, a UI or another instance:

turns.status(sessionId);                          // RUNNING under run-7, or IDLE with a stop reason
turns.interrupt(sessionId, "user pressed stop");  // ends the running turn

TurnService keeps no state. It reads and writes through the SessionService, so you can create one per call or keep one.

docs.title: What the log holds
docs.text:
Every change is an event in the session's log.

Event type Written when Payload TURN.STATUS A turn starts or ends status, runId, stopReason TURN.INTERRUPT Someone asks the running turn to stop reason TURN.QUESTION A turn stops to wait for an answer kind, value TURN.ANSWER The answer arrives and the turn goes on questionEventId, value

None of these events carries a message. The session's active view holds message events only, so these events never reach a prompt, and a compaction never covers them. They stay in the log as the record of the session's turns.

The status of a session is its newest TURN.STATUS event. A session without one is IDLE. There is no status column and no second store: the log is the only source.

docs.title: Status and stop reasons
docs.text:
A session is RUNNING while a turn runs, and IDLE otherwise. An idle session tells why its last turn ended:

Stop reason Meaning END_TURN The turn ran to its end. ERROR The turn failed. INTERRUPTED Someone called interrupt. A TURN.INTERRUPT event sits right before it. CANCELLED The client stopped listening, a cancelled stream for example. Nobody asked the session to stop, so there is no TURN.INTERRUPT event. REQUIRES_ACTION The turn is parked on a question and waits for an answer.

docs.title: How a change is written
docs.text:
Every method that changes the status follows the same steps. It reads the log's version, then the current status, and decides. Then it appends its events with the version it read. If another writer appended in between, the store refuses the append, and the method reads again and decides again. After five refused attempts it gives up with an IllegalStateException.

This is what makes two concurrent starts safe: both read the same version, both try to append, and the store accepts exactly one.

The activity of start:

flowchart TD
    A([start sessionId, runId]) --> B[Read the log's version]
    B --> C[Read the newest TURN.STATUS event]
    C --> D{Does a turn run?}
    D -- yes --> E([Throw TurnInProgressException<br/>with the running run id])
    D -- no --> F{Is the session parked?}
    F -- yes --> G([Throw TurnParkedException])
    F -- no --> H[Append TURN.STATUS RUNNING<br/>against the version read]
    H --> I{Did the store accept it?}
    I -- yes --> J([Return RUNNING under the run id])
    I -- no --> K{Fifth attempt?}
    K -- no --> B
    K -- yes --> L([Throw IllegalStateException])

end, interrupt, park and resume follow the same loop with their own decision:

  • end writes only when the turn runs under the caller's run id. Otherwise it writes nothing and returns the status as it stands. So a late end never overwrites a later turn, and an interrupt that landed first stands.
  • interrupt writes the TURN.INTERRUPT event and, when a turn runs, the TURN.STATUS event that ends it, in one append.
  • park and resume are described below.

docs.title: The types
docs.text:
classDiagram
    direction LR
    class TurnService {
        +TurnService(SessionService)
        +status(sessionId) TurnStatus
        +start(sessionId, runId) TurnStatus
        +end(sessionId, runId, StopReason) TurnStatus
        +interrupt(sessionId, reason) TurnStatus
        +park(sessionId, runId, Question) TurnStatus
        +pendingQuestion(sessionId) SessionEvent
        +resume(sessionId, runId, answer) TurnStatus
    }
    class TurnStatus {
        <<record>>
        +status SessionStatus
        +runId String
        +stopReason StopReason
        +isRunning() boolean
        +isParked() boolean
    }
    class SessionStatus {
        <<enumeration>>
        IDLE
        RUNNING
    }
    class StopReason {
        <<enumeration>>
        END_TURN
        ERROR
        INTERRUPTED
        CANCELLED
        REQUIRES_ACTION
    }
    class Question {
        <<record>>
        +kind String
        +payload Object
    }
    class Answer {
        <<record>>
        +questionEventId String
        +value Object
    }
    class ToolConfirmationQuestion {
        <<record>>
        +replyEventId String
        +toolCalls List
        +toQuestion() Question
    }
    class SessionService {
        <<interface>>
        +getEventVersion(sessionId) long
        +appendEvents(sessionId, events, version) boolean
        +getEvents(sessionId, filter) List
    }
    TurnService --> SessionService : reads and writes through
    TurnService ..> TurnStatus : returns
    TurnService ..> Question : parks on
    TurnStatus --> SessionStatus
    TurnStatus --> StopReason
    Answer ..> Question : answers
    ToolConfirmationQuestion ..> Question : converts to

SessionService is Spring AI's interface. TurnEventTypes holds the four event types, and SessionStatusEvents and QuestionEvents build and read the events. The diagram leaves those helpers out.

docs.title: A turn that waits for a person
docs.text:
A turn can stop to ask a person something and go on later with the answer, on any instance, after any delay. The first kind of question is a tool call that needs a person's confirmation.

  • park writes a TURN.QUESTION event and a TURN.STATUS event IDLE with REQUIRES_ACTION, in one append. The session is then parked. It holds no turn while the person thinks.
  • pendingQuestion returns the open question: the newest TURN.QUESTION event when no TURN.ANSWER follows it.
  • resume writes a TURN.ANSWER event that points at the question, and a TURN.STATUS event RUNNING, in one append. Only a parked session resumes, so the same answer sent twice resumes once.
  • start on a parked session throws TurnParkedException. A new turn would leave the question open.

ToolConfirmationQuestion is the shape for a tool confirmation: the event id of the stored reply, and its tool calls with the ones that wait for a decision. The answer is Spring AI's ToolCallDecisions.

A harness parks a turn and a UI resumes it:

sequenceDiagram
    participant H as Harness
    participant U as UI
    participant T as TurnService
    participant S as SessionService

    H->>T: start(sessionId, "run-1")
    T->>S: getEventVersion, newest TURN.STATUS
    T->>S: appendEvents [TURN.STATUS RUNNING]
    Note over H: the model asks for a tool<br/>that needs a confirmation
    H->>T: park(sessionId, "run-1", question)
    T->>S: appendEvents [TURN.QUESTION,<br/>TURN.STATUS IDLE REQUIRES_ACTION]
    Note over H,S: the harness may stop here, even restart
    U->>T: pendingQuestion(sessionId)
    T->>S: newest TURN.QUESTION or TURN.ANSWER
    T-->>U: the question
    U->>T: resume(sessionId, "run-2", decisions)
    T->>S: appendEvents [TURN.ANSWER,<br/>TURN.STATUS RUNNING]
    Note over U,S: the harness runs the allowed tools<br/>and the turn goes on

docs.title: What it does not do
docs.text:
• No lease. A turn whose harness died stays RUNNING until someone calls interrupt, which ends it. A later version can add a lease that lets the next start take over a turn that ran too long.
  • One answer per question. The answer decides every tool call of the question at once. An application that collects decisions one by one holds them until it has all.
  • No stop by itself. An interrupt changes the status. The harness that runs the turn learns of it only when it reads the status, between two model calls for example.
  • No transaction around it. Run the turn service outside a surrounding transaction. Inside one with repeatable read isolation, the version read does not see what another writer committed, and every attempt fails.
